component.name: (Local) AI Hub
component.summary: Control panel for the services you self-host

description.p: (Local) AI Hub is a free, open-source control panel for the services running on your own machine. Local AI comes first — Ollama, Open WebUI, ComfyUI, and any agent harness running on top of them — and below it sits everything else you self-host, found automatically from your rootless Podman containers. It puts them in one window so you don't need a terminal for day-to-day use.

ul.li: See what's running at a glance, with live status for each service.
Start and stop each tool with a single toggle.
Manage your models — update, install, and remove them.
See the address each service is reachable at, including from your phone.
Plain-language alerts when a service crashes, with a one-click log view.

description.p: Everything stays local. There's no account, no tracking, and no telemetry. The only network use is the model update checks, the downloads, and the version check you explicitly click.

It was built and verified on Bazzite with AMD Strix Halo hardware. Other setups are untested for now — the app is honest about what it can and can't detect on your machine, so services that aren't installed simply show as "Not installed" rather than erroring.

screenshot.caption: The hub in dark mode, showing running services and installed models

description.p: The app is now called (Local) AI Hub. This is a display name change only; the application ID and everything about an existing installation are unchanged.
Renames the second group to Self-Hosted Apps and Services, which says more clearly that it covers the services you host yourself rather than applications installed on the machine.
The app now covers everything you self-host, in two groups: Local AI on top, and Self-Hosted Apps and Services below, found automatically from your rootless Podman containers.
Each service shows the addresses it is actually reachable at, including your LAN and Tailscale, so you know what to type on a phone.
Fixes HTTPS in the AppImage and standalone builds on non-Debian systems, where the bundled OpenSSL found no certificate store and every network request failed verification.
Installing or removing a tool is now noticed while the app is running, so the "Not installed" state appears and disappears without a restart.
Agent harnesses that run on top of the stack get their own section, showing what they depend on and which model they are configured against. Hermes Agent is supported first.
Added a check for a newer version of the app, in the About panel. It contacts the network only when pressed, and never updates the app itself — Flatpak installs are pointed at their app store.
Relicensed under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0, and added an in-app license line to the About panel.
First public release of (Local) AI Hub.
